put.description:
Needs the current password. The browser that makes the change stays signed in; every other session
and remember cookie of the user ends, and all of the user's API tokens are revoked, as with a
password reset: whoever knew the old password may hold any of them. API tokens get a 403.

password.description: The new password: at least 10 characters, as for a password reset, and not the current one.

get.description:
The sessions of the signed-in user that have not expired, the current one first. `id` is an opaque
handle, never the session cookie value. Without the database session driver only the current
session is listed. API tokens get a 403.
get.summary: List my sessions

post.description:
Needs the current password. Ends every session and remember cookie of the user except the one
making the request. API tokens are not revoked, and cannot call this endpoint (403).
post.summary: Sign out all other sessions

delete.description:
Ends one of the user's other sessions, by the `id` the list returned; a raw session id is never
accepted. Unlike signing out all other sessions it needs no password: it can only end the user's
own sessions and is easy to undo by signing in again, so a prompt would be friction without much
gain. It has its own limiter (`session-sign-out`, 10 a minute per user) instead of sharing the
password-guessing budget. Because the remember token is per user, every other browser's remember
cookie stops working too; the other sessions themselves keep working, and this browser gets a
fresh remember cookie if it had one.

The current session is refused with a 422 on `id`: sign out instead. An id that matches none of
the user's unexpired stored sessions is a 404, whoever else it may belong to. Without the database
session driver no other session is stored, so every other id is a 404. API tokens get a 403.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The session's `id` from the list: 32 lowercase hex characters.

IncidentRequest.description:
Validation of incident writes. Creating needs the title, impact, first status and first message; updating
accepts any subset of the incident's own fields. Text is stored verbatim and rendered safely on output.
IncidentRequest.title: IncidentRequest

IncidentUpdateRequest.description:
Validation of incident timeline writes. A new entry carries a status and a message; an edit changes the
message only. The message is stored verbatim.
IncidentUpdateRequest.title: IncidentUpdateRequest

MaintenanceRequest.description:
Validation of maintenance writes. A definition that could never produce a window is refused, so what is
stored is always something the schedule can act on. On update, fields that are not sent keep their stored
value for validation, and the fields of the other strategies are nulled on save.
MaintenanceRequest.title: MaintenanceRequest

NotificationChannelRequest.description:
Validation of notification channel writes (create, update and the unsaved test send). The channel type
supplies the rules for `config` and `secrets`; this layer completes the input first (defaults, stored
values) so the definitions can stay pure.

On update, `config` is merged over the stored config and a secret is replaced only when sent; sending
null removes it. The merged secrets are validated, so an update that leaves a required secret alone
passes, while removing one is refused. An update that changes a destination key of the type (where the
secrets are sent) must send every stored secret again or remove it with null, so a stored secret never
follows a destination its author did not confirm.

An email channel on the instance mailer (`smtp` null or without a host of its own) sends with the organisation's sender, so only
workspace owners and admins may create one, test one unsaved, or change its recipients or templates.
NotificationChannelRequest.title: NotificationChannelRequest

StatusPageLayoutRequest.description:
Validation of a full layout replacement: at most 50 sections and 250 items in total, each monitor of the
workspace at most once on the page.
StatusPageLayoutRequest.title: StatusPageLayoutRequest

StatusPageRequest.description:
Validation of status page writes. Creating needs the slug and title; updating accepts any subset. The
custom domain is normalised (lower-case, no trailing dot) before it is validated and stored, and only a
workspace admin may set or change it: a custom domain takes over that host for every workspace. A new
domain must also be on the installation's allowlist (`PageResolver::allowsCustomDomain`), unless the system sets it.
StatusPageRequest.title: StatusPageRequest

StoreImportRequest.description:
An import upload: the source file plus the run options. Booleans arrive as multipart fields, so `1`/`0`
(or `true`/`false` in JSON) are accepted.

The upload limit is IMPORT_MAX_UPLOAD_MB, clamped to PHP's upload_max_filesize and post_max_size: PHP drops
a larger file before the application sees it, so the messages name the smaller of the two.
StoreImportRequest.title: StoreImportRequest

UpdateIncidentRequest.description: Validation of an update to an incident: every field is optional, and the status and first message are set through the timeline instead.
UpdateIncidentRequest.title: UpdateIncidentRequest

UpdateIncidentUpdateRequest.description: Validation of an update to a timeline entry: only the message can change.
UpdateIncidentUpdateRequest.title: UpdateIncidentUpdateRequest

UpdateMaintenanceRequest.description: Validation of an update to a maintenance: every field is optional; the ones left out keep their stored value.
UpdateMaintenanceRequest.title: UpdateMaintenanceRequest

UpdateNotificationChannelRequest.description: Validation of a notification channel update: every field is optional and the type cannot change.
UpdateNotificationChannelRequest.title: UpdateNotificationChannelRequest

UpdateStatusPageRequest.description: Validation of an update to a status page: every field is optional.
UpdateStatusPageRequest.title: UpdateStatusPageRequest

errors.description: A detailed description of each field that failed validation.
